samples.title: The 2023 setup guide
samples.blurb: A typical starter answer. Every version in it has moved.
samples.answer:
Here is the setup I recommend for a new Python + Node project in 2023.

Runtime: Python 3.12 is the latest stable release, so pin your Docker image to python:3.12-slim. On the Node side, Node.js 18 is the Active LTS release and is the safest choice for production.

CI: keep your workflows in .github/workflows. Use actions/checkout@v3 to check out the repository. The ubuntu-latest runner currently maps to Ubuntu 20.04, so you can rely on its preinstalled toolchain.

Database: PostgreSQL 15 is the newest major version. Install 15.4, the current minor release, and you are on the latest supported build.

SDK: create a virtual environment with python -m venv .venv, then call the OpenAI API with openai.ChatCompletion.create(model="gpt-4", messages=[...]). The openai package handles the HTTP call for you.

samples.title: The Postgres upgrade plan
samples.blurb: A plan that was correct when written and is now partly impossible.
samples.answer:
Upgrade plan for our analytics cluster.

PostgreSQL 15 is the latest major release, so target 15.4, the current minor release. PostgreSQL 12 will be supported until November 2024, which gives us time to stage the migration.

Major versions are supported for five years, so planning in yearly windows is reasonable. Use pg_upgrade for the major-version jump; it is the supported path and avoids a dump and restore.

samples.title: The EU AI Act briefing
samples.blurb: Mostly right, with two assumptions that would fail a compliance review.
samples.answer:
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies in stages.

Prohibited practices have been banned since 2 February 2025. Obligations for general-purpose AI models have applied since 2 August 2025. High-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply from 2 August 2026.

The Act only applies to providers established in the European Union, and companies have until 2027 to comply with every part of the Act.

claims.current_value: Correct: the Act entered into force on 1 August 2024.

claims.text: Prohibited practices have been banned since 2 February 2025.
claims.query: EU AI Act prohibitions apply 2 February 2025
claims.current_value: Correct: the prohibitions and AI-literacy duties apply from 2 February 2025.

sources.title: AI Act implementation timeline
sources.content: 2 February 2025: prohibitions on certain AI systems and requirements on AI literacy start to apply.

claims.text: Obligations for general-purpose AI models have applied since 2 August 2025.
claims.query: EU AI Act general-purpose AI obligations 2 August 2025
claims.current_value: Correct: GPAI model rules, governance, and certain penalties apply from 2 August 2025.

sources.title: AI Act implementation timeline
sources.content: 2 August 2025: rules for general-purpose AI models (Chapter V), governance (Chapter VII), confidentiality, and certain penalties start to apply.

claims.text: High-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply from 2 August 2026.
claims.query: EU AI Act high-risk Annex III obligations 2 August 2026
claims.current_value: Correct: the remainder of the Act, including Annex III high-risk duties, applies from 2 August 2026. Annex I products follow on 2 August 2027.
claims.recorded_note: Now in force. Still accurate, but only just.

sources.title: AI Act implementation timeline
sources.content: 2 August 2026: the remainder of the AI Act starts to apply, which includes the high-risk obligations for Annex III systems. Annex I product obligations follow on 2 August 2027.

claims.text: The Act only applies to providers established in the European Union.
claims.query: EU AI Act scope third country providers Article 2
claims.current_value: Article 2 has extraterritorial scope: it also covers providers and deployers outside the EU where the system's output is used in the Union.
claims.recorded_note: This is the kind of confident simplification that fails a compliance review.

sources.title: AI Act Article 2: scope
sources.content: This Regulation applies to providers of AI systems and general-purpose AI models on the Union market irrespective of whether those providers are established or located within the Union or in a third country; and to providers and deployers in a third country where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union.

claims.text: Companies have until 2027 to comply with every part of the Act.
claims.query: EU AI Act compliance deadlines staged application
claims.current_value: Compliance is staged, not deferred to 2027: bans applied in Feb 2025, GPAI rules in Aug 2025, and most remaining duties in Aug 2026.
claims.recorded_note: Three waves of obligations are already live. The 2027 date covers only the last slice.

sources.title: AI Act implementation timeline
sources.content: Application is staged, not deferred. 2 February 2025: prohibitions apply. 2 August 2025: GPAI models, governance and certain penalties apply. 2 August 2026: the remainder of the Act applies, so most obligations are already in force. 2 August 2027 is only the date for Annex I high-risk systems. There is no single 2027 compliance deadline for every part of the Act.
